c_Audit_Cascades.md¶

Conditions Substrate Model — Cascade Detection Audit Procedures¶

1. Identity¶

Module: Conditions Substrate Model
Role: Cascade Audit Layer
Purpose: Provide formal audit procedures for verifying multi‑dimension drift cascades, threshold chains, hook alignment, propagation loops, and regime correctness.

Cascade audits ensure system‑level accuracy in the highest‑order instability patterns.

2. Cascade Audit Architecture¶

Cascade audits operate across six layers:

Layer 1 — Drift Dominance Audit
Layer 2 — Coherence Break Audit
Layer 3 — Threshold Chain Audit
Layer 4 — Hook Alignment Audit
Layer 5 — Propagation Loop Audit
Layer 6 — Regime Outcome Audit

Each layer must pass for a cascade to be considered valid.

3. Layer 1 — Drift Dominance Audit¶

A cascade requires multiple dimensions where:

[
Drift(d_i) > Coherence(d_i)
]

Audit Checklist¶

[ ] Drift(d) computed correctly
[ ] Coherence(d) computed correctly
[ ] Drift(d) > Coherence(d) for ≥ 2 dimensions
[ ] Drift vector direction consistent with modifiers

Failure Modes¶

  • Drift miscalculated
  • Coherence envelope too high
  • Only one dimension exceeds coherence → Not a cascade

Severity¶

  • Incorrect drift → Major
  • Missing drift dimension → Critical

4. Layer 2 — Coherence Break Audit¶

A cascade requires coherence collapse across dimensions.

Audit Checklist¶

[ ] Coherence(d) < CoherenceThreshold(d)
[ ] Coherence(d) decreasing across time steps
[ ] Coherence(d) not artificially inflated by stabilizing fields

Failure Modes¶

  • Stabilizing fields not accounted for
  • Coherence miscalculated
  • Coherence break detected in only one dimension

Severity¶

  • Incorrect coherence → Major
  • Missing coherence break → Critical

5. Layer 3 — Threshold Chain Audit¶

Cascades follow canonical threshold chains:

narrow → oscillate → destabilize → collapse

Audit Checklist¶

[ ] narrow_threshold crossed
[ ] oscillate_threshold crossed
[ ] destabilize_threshold crossed
[ ] chain ordering correct
[ ] chain acceleration detected (multiple thresholds at once)

Failure Modes¶

  • Missing oscillate threshold
  • Destabilize threshold triggered prematurely
  • Incorrect threshold ordering

Severity¶

  • Incorrect ordering → Critical
  • Missing threshold → Catastrophic

6. Layer 4 — Hook Alignment Audit¶

Hooks amplify drift and synchronize cascades.

Audit Checklist¶

[ ] HookGain(d) computed correctly
[ ] Hooks activated across ≥ 2 dimensions
[ ] Hook alignment detected (e.g., cognitive_load + time_gate)
[ ] Hook conflicts resolved (stabilizing vs destabilizing)

Failure Modes¶

  • Missing hook activation
  • Incorrect hook alignment
  • Stabilizing hooks ignored

Severity¶

  • Incorrect hook alignment → Critical
  • Missing hook → Major

7. Layer 5 — Propagation Loop Audit¶

Propagation loops amplify cascades:

Media → Temporal → Governance → Media
Economic → Governance → Media → Economic
Infrastructure → Media → Emergency → Infrastructure

Audit Checklist¶

[ ] Propagation targets correct
[ ] Module gain G_module(d) applied correctly
[ ] Loop detected (≥ 2 modules feeding each other)
[ ] Loop direction consistent with drift vector

Failure Modes¶

  • Incorrect propagation target
  • Missing loop
  • Loop direction reversed

Severity¶

  • Missing loop → Critical
  • Incorrect propagation → Major

8. Layer 6 — Regime Outcome Audit¶

The final regime must match the cascade pattern.

Audit Checklist¶

[ ] Regime matches threshold chain
[ ] Regime matches drift/coherence balance
[ ] Regime matches hook alignment
[ ] Regime matches propagation loop

Failure Modes¶

  • Regime misclassified
  • Regime inconsistent with drift
  • Regime inconsistent with thresholds

Severity¶

  • Incorrect regime → Critical
  • Cascade misidentified → Catastrophic

9. Cascade Audit Examples¶

Example A — Informational–Temporal Cascade¶

Issue: D1 + D3 drift detected, D7 ignored
Severity: Critical
Fix: Recompute drift vector → rebuild cascade

Example B — Governance Collapse Cascade¶

Issue: oscillate_threshold(D7) skipped
Severity: Critical
Fix: re-evaluate thresholds → update regime

Example C — Economic Shock Cascade¶

Issue: propagation loop missing (Economic → Governance → Media)
Severity: Major
Fix: rebuild propagation map

10. Cascade Audit Severity Matrix¶

Severity Description Required Operator Action
Minor Single-dimension misalignment Correct and re‑compute
Major Drift/coherence imbalance Full drift/coherence recalculation
Critical Threshold chain failure Reconstruct regime logic
Catastrophic Cascade undetected Full multi‑layer audit

1. Identity¶

Module: Conditions Substrate Model
Role: Finance Regime Layer
Purpose: Define canonical regime states for financial substrates, including stability envelopes, drift‑dominant states, oscillation engines, scarcity regimes, and collapse modes.

Finance substrates exhibit high drift gain, low coherence, and rapid threshold chains.

2. Finance Regime Structure¶

A finance regime is defined as:

[
FinanceRegime = (DriftVector,\; CoherenceEnvelope,\; ThresholdChain,\; PropagationLoops)
]

Where:

  • DriftVector — directional deviation across D5, D1, D7, D0, D3
  • CoherenceEnvelope — stabilizing fields (governance, clarity, cohesion)
  • ThresholdChain — narrow → oscillate → destabilize → collapse
  • PropagationLoops — cross‑substrate amplification (markets → media → governance → markets)

3. Canonical Finance Regimes¶

Below are the canonical finance‑substrate regimes recognized by the Conditions Substrate Model.

3.1 Regime: Stable Finance**¶

Definition¶

A high‑coherence financial environment with low drift and strong stabilizing fields.

Characteristics¶

Drift(D5) = low
Coherence(D5) = high
Thresholds: none crossed
Propagation: minimal

Indicators¶

  • predictable incentives
  • low volatility
  • strong governance legitimacy
  • clear informational channels

Notes¶

Stable finance is the baseline regime.

3.2 Regime: Expanded Finance**¶

Definition¶

A growth‑oriented regime with expanding incentives and strong governance + clarity.

Characteristics¶

Drift(D5) = expanding
Coherence(D5) = high
Thresholds: expand_threshold(D5)
Propagation: positive reinforcement loops

Indicators¶

  • sustained investment
  • high liquidity
  • strong coordination
  • clarity‑driven stabilization

Notes¶

Expansion requires aligned governance + clarity + cohesion.

3.3 Regime: Narrowed Finance**¶

Definition¶

A scarcity‑driven regime where drift exceeds coherence but oscillation has not yet begun.

Characteristics¶

Drift(D5) > Coherence(D5)
Thresholds: narrow_threshold(D5)
Propagation: scarcity loops

Indicators¶

  • liquidity stress
  • resource scarcity
  • tightening credit
  • rising default risk

Notes¶

Narrowing is the first stage of collapse chains.

3.4 Regime: Oscillating Finance**¶

Definition¶

A volatility‑driven regime where oscillation thresholds are crossed.

Characteristics¶

Drift(D5) = high
Coherence(D5) = low
Thresholds: oscillate_threshold(D5)
Propagation: volatility loops

Indicators¶

  • rapid price swings
  • margin call cascades
  • unstable incentives
  • media amplification

Notes¶

Oscillation is the canonical finance drift signature.

3.5 Regime: Destabilized Finance**¶

Definition¶

A regime where volatility + scarcity + governance instability synchronize.

Characteristics¶

Drift(D5) >> Coherence(D5)
Thresholds: destabilize_threshold(D5)
Propagation: multi‑substrate cascades

Indicators¶

  • credit freeze
  • liquidity collapse
  • governance instability
  • narrative fragmentation

Notes¶

Destabilization is the pre‑collapse regime.

3.6 Regime: Collapsed Finance**¶

Definition¶

A full‑scale financial collapse where multiple dimensions exceed coherence simultaneously.

Characteristics¶

Drift(D5) = extreme
Coherence(D5) = near-zero
Thresholds: collapse_threshold(D5)
Propagation: synchronized cascades across D0, D1, D7, D2

Indicators¶

  • multi‑sector failure
  • synchronized global cascades
  • governance coordination collapse
  • panic selling + liquidity freeze

Notes¶

Collapse is the terminal regime of the finance substrate.

4. Cross‑Dimension Finance Regimes¶

Finance regimes often involve multiple dimensions:

D5 + D1 (Economic + Informational)¶

  • volatility + overload
  • panic cascades
  • oscillation engines

D5 + D7 (Economic + Governance)¶

  • rule instability
  • legitimacy drift
  • destabilization cascades

D5 + D0 (Economic + Structural)¶

  • clearing bottlenecks
  • throughput collapse

D5 + D2 (Economic + Emotional)¶

  • fear‑driven selling
  • resonance spirals

5. Threshold Chains in Finance¶

Finance substrates follow the canonical threshold chain:

narrow(D5)
→ oscillate(D5)
→ destabilize(D5)
→ collapse(D5)

Audit Notes¶

  • oscillate_threshold(D5) is the most commonly missed
  • collapse_threshold(D5) requires multi‑dimension drift

6. Propagation Loops in Finance¶

Finance cascades propagate through:

Loop A — Markets → Media → Governance → Markets¶

  • volatility → overload → opacity → volatility

Loop B — Markets → Infrastructure → Markets¶

  • clearing bottleneck → liquidity freeze → clearing bottleneck

Loop C — Markets → Emotions → Media → Markets¶

  • fear → amplification → panic → fear

These loops define cascade acceleration.

7. Regime Detection Logic¶

A finance regime is detected when:

[
Regime = f(Drift(d), Coherence(d), ThresholdChain, PropagationLoops)
]

Detection Steps¶

  1. Compute Drift(D5)
  2. Compute Coherence(D5)
  3. Check threshold chain
  4. Identify propagation loops
  5. Assign regime

Conditions Substrate Model — Planet‑Scale Regime Definitions¶

1. Identity¶

2. Planetary Regime Structure¶

]

→ C1 gains propagation(d)

Propagation determines cross‑substrate effects.

Builds multi‑condition stacks.

Stack = {C_1, C_2, …, C_k}
]

[
GlobalCascade = \bigcap_{i=1}^{k} { Drift(d_i) > Coherence(d_i) }

Gradientary — Propagation Dictionary (Volume VII)¶

0. Identity¶

Module: Gradientary
Role: Propagation Lexicon
Purpose: Provide dictionary‑grade definitions for all propagation classes: vectors, webs, loops, synchronizations, envelopes, and cross‑substrate flows across dimensional, civilizational, planetary, epochal, and deep‑time layers.

Propagation is the movement of the canon — how drift travels, how coherence spreads, how cascades expand.

1. Propagation Entry Format¶

propagation: <canonical name>
type: <vector | web | loop | synchronization | envelope | composite>
definition: <minimal canonical definition>
equation: <if applicable>
notes: <diagnostic or structural notes>

2. Propagation Vectors (P‑Vectors)¶

prop.vector.basic¶

type: vector
definition: directional flow across a single substrate
equation: Prop(d) = C(d) · G(d)
notes: base propagation operator

prop.vector.multi¶

type: vector
definition: multi‑substrate propagation vector
equation: {Prop(D0)…Prop(D7)}
notes: cross‑substrate flow

prop.vector.collapse¶

type: vector
definition: collapse propagation vector
equation: {D0→D7→D1→D5}
notes: collapse arc

prop.vector.coherence¶

type: vector
definition: coherence propagation vector
equation: {D7→D1→D4→D0}
notes: stability arc

3. Propagation Webs (P‑Webs)¶

prop.web.collapse¶

type: web
definition: biosphere→governance→media→economics→biosphere
equation: D0→D7→D1→D5→D0
notes: planetary collapse topology

prop.web.civilization¶

type: web
definition: civilization→infrastructure→media→governance→civilization
equation: D4→D0→D1→D7→D4
notes: civilizational arc topology

prop.web.info-governance-social¶

type: web
definition: narrative→legitimacy→cohesion loop
equation: D1→D7→D4→D1
notes: oscillation loop

prop.web.coherence¶

type: web
definition: governance→clarity→cohesion→stability
equation: D7→D1→D4→D0
notes: coherence topology

4. Propagation Loops (P‑Loops)¶

prop.loop.oscillation¶

type: loop
definition: informational→governance→economic→social→informational
equation: D1→D7→D5→D4→D1
notes: volatility loop

prop.loop.stability¶

type: loop
definition: governance→clarity→cohesion→governance
equation: D7→D1→D4→D7
notes: stability loop

prop.loop.collapse¶

type: loop
definition: structural→governance→informational→economic→structural
equation: D0→D7→D1→D5→D0
notes: collapse loop

5. Propagation Synchronizations (P‑Sync)¶

prop.sync.drift¶

type: synchronization
definition: synchronized drift propagation across substrates
equation: Prop(d_i) == Prop(d_j)
notes: collapse precursor

prop.sync.coherence¶

type: synchronization
definition: synchronized coherence propagation
equation: Coh(d_i) == Coh(d_j)
notes: stability precursor

prop.sync.cascade¶

type: synchronization
definition: synchronized drift + coherence + hook propagation
equation: Drift==Coh==Hook
notes: cascade ignition

6. Propagation Envelopes (P‑Envelopes)¶

prop.envelope.collapse¶

type: envelope
definition: collapse propagation envelope
equation: Prop(D0,D7,D1,D5)↑↑↑
notes: G7 signature

prop.envelope.coherence¶

type: envelope
definition: coherence propagation envelope
equation: Prop(D7,D1,D4,D0)↑↑
notes: stability signature

prop.envelope.oscillation¶

type: envelope
definition: oscillation propagation envelope
equation: Prop(D1,D7,D5)↑↑
notes: volatility signature

7. Composite Propagation (Cross‑Scale)¶

prop.composite.planetary¶

type: composite
definition: planetary propagation across D0,D1,D5,D7
equation: Prop_global = Σ Prop(d)
notes: planetary cascade engine

prop.composite.civilization¶

type: composite
definition: civilization propagation across C‑D0…C‑D7
equation: Prop_civ = Σ Prop(C‑D)
notes: civilizational cascade engine

prop.composite.epoch¶

type: composite
definition: epoch propagation across collapse→coherence chains
equation: Prop_epoch = Prop(E0…E7)
notes: epochal cascade engine

prop.composite.deep-time¶

type: composite
definition: propagation across meta‑epochs, biospheric arcs, geological regimes
equation: Prop_DT = Prop(M) + Prop(B) + Prop(GEO)
notes: deep‑time cascade engine

8. Propagation Chains (Canonical Flow Sequences)¶

chain.propagation.collapse¶

D0 → D7 → D1 → D5 → D0
notes: collapse arc

chain.propagation.regeneration¶

D0 → D7 → D1 → D4
notes: regeneration arc

chain.propagation.coherence¶

D7 → D1 → D4 → D0
notes: stability arc

chain.propagation.oscillation¶

D1 → D7 → D5 → D4
notes: volatility arc

chain.propagation.narrowing¶

D0 → D5 → D1 → D7
notes: scarcity arc

Propagation is:

  • the circulation system of the Conditions Substrate Model

Worked Examples — Conditions Substrate Model¶

TriadicFrameworks Canon (2026.07)

This page provides worked examples demonstrating how drift, coherence, resonance, hooks, thresholds, propagation, cycles, and cascades behave across substrates (D0–D7).
Each example is designed to show operator‑safe, canon‑aligned, regime‑aware reasoning.

1. Drift → Coherence Stabilization Example¶

Scenario:
A D3 substrate (organizational alignment) begins drifting toward D5 (resource scarcity).

Process:
- Drift signature: D3 → D4 → D5
- Coherence envelope: C4 attempts stabilization
- Threshold T5 triggers when drift velocity exceeds coherence capacity
- Propagation vector P3 carries instability into adjacent substrates
- Cycle C2 resets partial alignment

Outcome:
Coherence stabilizes only after drift velocity drops below T5, restoring D3 alignment.

2. Resonance Amplification Example¶

Scenario:
A resonance loop forms between D2 (communication substrate) and D6 (stress substrate).

Process:
- Resonance signature R2 activates
- Hook H6 binds stress feedback into communication loops
- Amplification occurs when R2 × H6 > threshold T6
- Cascade CA2 triggers cross‑substrate escalation

Outcome:
Resonance loop collapses only after hook alignment is broken via C4 coherence intervention.

3. Hook Activation Chain Example¶

Scenario:
A scarcity hook (H5) activates during a D4 substrate transition.

Process:
- Hook H5 aligns with drift signature D4
- Threshold T4 opens
- Propagation vector P4 carries scarcity into D3 and D6
- Cascade CA4 initiates multi‑substrate chain

Outcome:
Scarcity hook deactivates once propagation vectors are dampened by coherence envelope C3.

4. Threshold Inflection Example¶

Scenario:
A system approaches threshold T7 (high‑stress inflection).

Process:
- Drift velocity increases
- Coherence envelope C7 compresses
- Threshold T7 opens
- Regime shift R7 occurs
- Cascade CA7 triggers deep‑time cycle C7

Outcome:
System transitions into a new regime arc until drift velocity returns below T7.

5. Propagation Web Example¶

Scenario:

A cycle engine C4 repeats every 7 units.

- Coherence envelope C4 stabilizes mid‑cycle
- Resonance R4 amplifies cycle peak
- Threshold T4 closes cycle
- Deep‑time cycle C4 recurs

Outcome:

7. Cascade Transition Example¶

Scenario:
A dimensional cascade CA1 transitions into a composite cascade CA3.

- Propagation vector P1 carries signal upward
- Composite cascade CA3 forms when P1 intersects P3
- Regime shift R3 occurs
- Coherence envelope C3 stabilizes post‑cascade

Outcome:
Cascade resolves once composite vectors lose synchronization.

Operator Notes: collapse precursor; stability anchor

Operator Notes: overload ignition; coherence engine

# c_Template.md

Canonical Module Template — TriadicFrameworks¶

This file provides the standard structural scaffold for any TriadicFrameworks module.
Use it when creating new modules or refreshing existing ones.

1. Identity¶

Module:
Category:
Purpose:
Version: 2026.07
Front door: /docs//

2. Roles (TriadicFrameworks Grammar)¶

  • engine — core logic or substrate model
  • profile — dimensional or substrate-specific mapping
  • signature — canonical signatures
  • diagnostic — thresholds, audits, diff tables
  • map — atlases, flows, vectors
  • example — worked examples
  • extension — optional expansions
  • index — front door / capture page
  • reference — dictionaries, glossaries
  • template — this file

3. Analyzer Layers¶

  • operator
  • dimensional
  • regime
  • drift
  • coherence
  • cross-cutting

Enable layers as needed in module.json.

4. Canonical Blocks¶

Each module includes:

  • Metadata block (c_Metadata.html)
  • Session context (c_Session_Context.html)
  • Badge (c_Badge.html)
  • Sidebar audit (c_Sidebar_Audit.html)
  • Diff table (c_Diff_Table.html)
  • module.json
  • modules_group.json
  • sitemap_entry.xml

These blocks are required for canonical compliance.

5. File Structure (example)¶

/docs/<module_name>/
  c_Capture.md
  c_Metadata.html
  c_Session_Context.html
  c_Badge.html
